clue.text: Schedule about to allow use of a river

blocks.note: ca. (circa) is the abbreviation for about
to lend something is to allow another person the use of it
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A timetable fixing when boats may use a stretch of river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'Schedule' with 'allow use', but CA, LEND, A and R simply run on in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a list of dated events or appointments, a programme in noun form much like a schedule.

clue.text: One losing faith in a semi-impoverished condition

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the following word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
impoverished people are poor; only its first half is kept
a state is a condition, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning their religion while living in near poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-impoverished' reads as one adjective, but it splits into a halving signal and the word it halves.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is a person who renounces a religious belief, so is one who has lost or abandoned their faith.

clue.text: What could make Beckie sexier, or fitter?

definitions.text: What could make Beckie sexier, or fitter?

indicators.note: asks what these letters could be made into, inviting a rearrangement

blocks.note: the twelve letters of the two words, used together

explanation.surface: Wondering what would improve Beckie's figure or fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: Beckie sexier rearranges into the answer, and the question as a whole describes that machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationary bicycle used for workouts, the sort of gym machine that tones a body and improves health.

clue.text: Catcher left free to watch from below, catching a break

indicators.note: in a down answer, reading from below means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards
one thing catching another holds it inside itself

blocks.note: to tend a flock is to watch over it
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A baseball catcher left unmarked so he can watch the play from low down, catching a lucky break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catcher' looks like a person; it is a fishing net, and 'left free' belongs to the definition because such a net is not anchored.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift net is a large fishing net left to float freely with the current, trapping the fish that swim into it.

clue.text: I'm transformed with green therapeutic course

indicators.note: something transformed has been changed into a different form

blocks.note: the two letters, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that a green, eco-friendly treatment has changed their life.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed plan of diet, exercise or medication followed to improve health.

clue.text: Extremists in federal Europe conspire to swindle

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are the letters at its two ends

blocks.note: its first and last letters
its first and last letters
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Political radicals inside a federal Europe plot to cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' suggests political fanatics, but it only means the end letters of the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is slang for cheating them out of money, as a sheep is stripped of its wool.

clue.text: Prison time not showing a drop

indicators.note: what is not showing has gone from view, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: a jail is a prison
T is the abbreviation for time
the letter that goes missing

explanation.surface: A prison stretch that somehow leaves no visible weight loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison time' reads as one sentence; it is JAIL plus T, and then the A leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To jilt a lover is to abandon or reject them abruptly, a sense of drop as a verb.

clue.text: Crete developed in cunning and in confidence

indicators.note: something developed has grown into a new shape
one part is placed in the other

blocks.note: sly means cunning
the island's letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek island quietly and craftily developed by speculators.
explanation.walkthrough: Crete is only letters to be rearranged; they go inside the word for cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something secretly means doing it privately, away from others, which is what in confidence describes.

clue.text: Rave about reduced computer access in start of electronic application

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
reduced means made shorter, so a letter is lopped off the end
one part is placed within the other

blocks.note: the opening letter
a login is the act or details for gaining access to a computer
an application is a use, as in the application of a rule

explanation.surface: Someone enthusing about a cut-down way of logging in to an electronic app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' looks like an app on a device, but it means putting something to use.
explanation.definitionFit: To eulogise something is to praise it highly, which is what raving about it in admiration does.

clue.text: Blessed, ultimately, almost more than peacemaker

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter is wanted
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: its final letter
over means more than, as in over fifty people

explanation.surface: A nod to 'Blessed are the peacemakers', suggesting someone almost more blessed than they.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatitudes echo makes 'Blessed' feel like a definition; it supplies only its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dove is a symbol of peace and a name for a politician who favours conciliation over war.

clue.text: Appliance set up in pass on a rocky height

indicators.note: one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: to refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else
to rig is to set up equipment
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Equipment hauled up to a mountain pass on a craggy peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' reads as a mountain pass; it is the verb to pass on.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator is a household device for keeping food cold, a standard kitchen appliance.

clue.text: Skimmed revenue managed most of a certain unspecified fortune

indicators.note: skimmed means with the top taken off, so the first letter goes
most of a word is all but its last letter

blocks.note: takings are a shop's revenue
to run a business is to manage it
some means a certain, as in some person

explanation.surface: Someone skimming money from a business they ran and making a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skimmed revenue' suggests embezzlement, but it only removes the top letter of a word for revenue.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a very large but unstated sum of money, enough to free a captured monarch.

clue.text: Harmful side on motorway

indicators.note: in an across answer, putting one thing on another places it after, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
to side with someone is to align with them

explanation.surface: A dangerous stretch at the edge of the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' reads as a noun; it is the verb, as in taking sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign describes something evil in nature or effect, such as a malign influence that causes damage.

clue.text: Faculty express despair in English, still

indicators.note: one part is placed within the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
yet means still, as in yet more
a sigh expresses despair

explanation.surface: A university department still sighing in despair in the English school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' suggests a university department; it means a bodily power.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the power of seeing, one of the senses, which are called faculties.

clue.text: People behind the writer, against a trophy

indicators.note: behind puts the first-named piece after the one that follows it in the clue

blocks.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as me
men are people
to can mean against, as in back to back

explanation.surface: A team behind the writer, competing against them for a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts the people after the writer; then 'against' adds the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake kept in memory of an event, which is what a trophy can be.

clue.text: Fashion shopper getting round at a medium pace

blocks.note: a mode is a fashion
to shop someone is to inform on them, and an informer is a rat
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A fashion shopper moving around the boutiques at a steady speed.
explanation.walkthrough: A shopper here is not a customer but someone who shops, British slang for informing on, a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderato is the Italian tempo marking in music for playing at a moderate speed.

clue.text: Let us get past customary behaviour of organised criminals?

blocks.note: first meaning: a shout to clear a path through a crowd
second meaning, whimsical: the usual way of a criminal mob

explanation.surface: A plea to be allowed past the routines of the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a pun: a gang's way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangway is shouted to make people stand aside, and split in two it means the way, or custom, of a gang.

clue.text: Source of excitement in Australian patronage

indicators.note: one part is placed within the other

blocks.note: Aus is the abbreviation for Australian
spice is what makes something exciting, as in the spice of life

explanation.surface: Something thrilling about being sponsored in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices of someone means with their backing or support, which is a form of patronage.

clue.text: About time that Browning is seen and leaves shed?

definitions.text: About time that Browning is seen and leaves shed?

blocks.clueFragment: About time that Browning is seen
blocks.note: surface reading: overdue that the poet Robert Browning got some attention
setter's reading: relating to the season when foliage turns brown and trees drop it

explanation.walkthrough: The capital B and 'About time' suggest a poet long ignored; 'About' means relating to, and the browning is of foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of or relating to the season of fall, when leaves change colour and drop.

clue.text: Criticise screen shot that's gripping for any audience

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so its letters are broken up
a thing gripping another holds it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: Condemning a gripping film scene that has been passed as suitable for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screen shot' reads as one image; the screen's letters are shot, and U is the British universal film rating.
explanation.definitionFit: To censure is to express strong formal disapproval of someone, a severe kind of criticism.

clue.text: Water falling in Land's End: time for way of removing it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: its final letter
rain is water falling from the sky
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Rain at Cornwall's tip needs a way to clear it.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of Cornwall, but here it only means the last letter of Land; 'it' in the definition points back to the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainage is the system or process for carrying away surplus water from land or buildings.

clue.text: Fletcher's employer could be more mischievous

blocks.note: first meaning: a fletcher makes arrows, for a bowman to shoot
second meaning: the comparative of arch, meaning playfully roguish

explanation.walkthrough: Fletcher looks like a surname; a fletcher is an arrow-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowman uses what the arrow-maker makes, and arch, roguishly knowing, compares with -er.

clue.text: Small dog's run inside, little squirt!

indicators.note: one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: the spitz is a small breed of dog with a pointed muzzle
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A tiny dog runs indoors, the little brat!
explanation.walkthrough: 'little squirt' sounds like an insult to the dog; it is a small spray.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritz is a short spray of liquid, such as a squirt of perfume or soda water.

clue.text: Consequence related to striking

blocks.note: re means concerning or with reference to
percussion is the striking of one thing against another

explanation.surface: An outcome connected to industrial strike action.
explanation.definitionFit: A repercussion is an unintended after-effect of an action, a result that follows from it.

clue.text: Regular servings of porridge? Goody-goody!

indicators.note: regular servings are helpings at even intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A child delighted at being given porridge every day.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is also British slang for prison time, but here it only supplies alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A prig is a self-righteous person, smugly concerned with being correct, which is a goody-goody.

clue.text: Family member with grand air

blocks.note: a son is a member of a family
G is short for grand, slang for a thousand

explanation.surface: A relative who gives himself grand airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand air' reads as haughtiness; 'air' means a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody or tune, so a song is the same musical sense.

clue.text: Sign of punishment, not fine musical appreciation

blocks.note: thick is the opposite of fine, as of thread or hair
to have an ear for music is to appreciate it

explanation.surface: A musical punishment not involving a fine, perhaps for poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: A thick ear is British for an ear swollen from a cuff on the head, once a common rough punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The swelling left by a slap to the side of the head shows that someone has been chastised.

clue.text: Some Yeomen's emblematic outfit

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a run of their letters is used

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: The ceremonial uniform worn by some Yeomen of the Guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen of the Guard are the Beefeaters at the Tower of London, famous for their outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a set of clothes chosen to be worn together, a coordinated outfit.
